sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The deck and slide questions use BFS in contexts that can mean either best-first search or breadth-first search.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Spell out greedy best-first search and breadth-first search on every audience-facing page; reserve abbreviations only after disambiguation.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: Open is described as a max or min heap and Closed as a queue even though lower h values are preferred.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use a min-priority queue for Open under the deck's score convention and a set or best-known-cost map for Closed.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The archival pseudocode tracks shorter paths but the presenter note says the returned current path becomes the shortest path after any solution is found.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Greedy best-first search is not optimal merely because parent links or best-known duplicate paths are maintained; optimality requires the appropriate f ordering and A* assumptions.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The slide annotation uses h*(n) for an estimate that never overestimates, whereas standard notation uses h*(n) for the true optimal remaining cost.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use h*(n) as true remaining cost and define admissibility as 0 less than or equal to h(n) less than or equal to h*(n), with h(goal)=0.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The slides mix heuristic admissibility with algorithm completeness and optimality and state that all A* algorithms are admissible without graph-search qualifications.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Separate heuristic admissibility from algorithm guarantees; state nonnegative-cost and termination assumptions, and explain that graph-search A* with an inconsistent heuristic may need to reopen states.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: Breadth-first search is described as admissible without the cost condition.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Breadth-first search is complete under standard finite-branching assumptions and optimal only when step costs are equal; uniform-cost search handles varying positive costs.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: Dijkstra is presented as an unconditional special case of A*.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: State that A* with h equals zero reduces to uniform-cost or Dijkstra-style search under nonnegative edge-cost assumptions.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The annotations call consistency local admissibility of h* and mix true-cost and estimated-cost notation.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use h(n) less than or equal to c(n,n-prime) plus h(n-prime), with h(goal)=0; explain that consistency implies nondecreasing f along a path and, under standard conditions, admissibility.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The slide says a more informed heuristic is better without immediately stating the admissibility and computation-cost conditions.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Compare pointwise dominance only among admissible heuristics and retain the source deck's explicit search-savings versus heuristic-computation tradeoff.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The bibliography misspells George F. Luger as George Fluger and Russell as Russel.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Use George F. Luger and Stuart Russell while preserving the original editions and chapter references.
